extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of periodical essays; literate general public interested in manners, humour, and moral instruction (early-18th-century Spectator audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for composing moralizing, humorous essays and satire for a general readership — how to use ridicule, character-types, tone, and form to instruct or amuse without corrupting. Also includes prescriptive social counsel (nursing, pastimes, domestic entertainments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent human nature fully to instruct the virtuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Without presenting Vice under any false alluring Notions, they give my Reader an Insight into the Ways of Men, and represent human Nature in all its changeable Colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of these papers is to let the virtuous and innocent know in speculation what they could not learn by practice, thereby opening their minds without vitiating them; do not glamorize vice when portraying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making virtue ridiculous through naive simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Man is made up wholly of the Dove, without the least Grain of the Serpent in his Composition, he becomes ridiculous in many Circumstances of Life, and very often discredits his best Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer should portray the ways of the world so that virtuous people gain competent knowledge of social practice; instruction should protect the innocent from being discredited by ignorance of social craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend innocent, domestic amusements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sports and Pastimes should be not only merry but innocent, suitable to pass away a Winter Night for those who do not care to throw away their Time at an Opera, or at the Play-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest indoor family entertainments (e.g. Questions and Commands, Mottoes, Similes, Cross-Purposes, Blind-Man's Buff) that are merry, wholesome, and suitable for wives/daughters and masters of families; explicitly exclude vices like Whisk, Lanterloo, One and Thirty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children ought to be nursed by their mothers when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: I beg of you, for the Sake of the many poor Infants that may and will be saved, by weighing this Case seriously, to exhort the People with the utmost Vehemence to let the Children suck their own Mothers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: nurses commonly corrupt children's health and temper; mother's milk benefits both mother and child (strengthens mother, prevents vapours/miscarriages; children thrive). Use as moral/practical counsel for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify female orators by rhetorical function
rubrics_metrics.description: The first kind ... are those who are employed in stirring up the Passions; the second kind deal in Invectives (the Censorious); a third kind are Gossips ... a fourth is the Coquet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting or analysing conversation/characters, identify types (passion-stirrers, invectives/censorious, gossips, coquets) and use their traits as humorous or critical material in essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tune speech by good qualities — avoid certain disagreeable notes
rubrics_metrics.description: All that I aim at by this Dissertation is, to cure it of several disagreeable Notes, and in particular of those little Jarrings and Dissonances which arise from Anger, Censoriousness, Gossiping and Coquetry. In short, I would always have it tuned by Good-Nature, Truth, Discretion and Sincerity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive standard for public and private discourse: encourage good-nature, truth, discretion and sincerity; discourage anger, censoriousness, gossip and affectation when portraying or advising about speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ridicule to correct vice/folly, not to attack virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Talent of Ridicule were employed to laugh Men out of Vice and Folly, it might be of some Use to the World; but instead of this, we find that it is generally made use of to laugh Men out of Virtue and good Sense, by attacking every thing that is Solemn and Praiseworthy in Human Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire/humour should aim at reforming vice and folly; avoid mean-spirited ridicule that derides solemn or praiseworthy conduct. A moralizing comic writer must distinguish targets carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the two great branches of literary ridicule: Comedy and Burlesque
rubrics_metrics.description: The two great Branches of Ridicule in Writing are Comedy and Burlesque. The first ridicules Persons by drawing them in their proper Characters, the other by drawing them quite unlike themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comedy when exposing a person's character as it is; use burlesque when representing a person out of character. This classification guides choice of technique and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose meter/style in burlesque according to aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Burlesque is of two kinds; the first represents mean Persons in the Accoutrements of Heroes, the other describes great Persons acting and speaking like the basest among the People. I think where the low Character is to be raised, the Heroick is the proper Measure; but when an Hero is to be pulled down and degraded, it is done best in Doggerel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule for satirists/poets: raise a low subject by employing heroic verse; pull down a lofty subject by using doggerel; match form to the intended comic reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor looseness and freedom of the essay form for new subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: When I make Choice of a Subject that has not been treated on by others, I throw together my Reflections on it without any Order or Method, so that they may appear rather in the Looseness and Freedom of an Essay, than in the Regularity of a Set Discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original or lightly-treated topics, adopt an informal, discursive style rather than rigid method; allow reflective looseness to suit the essayistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making ridicule the principal claim to wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Talent of turning Men into Ridicule, and exposing to Laughter those one converses with, is the Qualification of little ungenerous Tempers. A young Man with this Cast of Mind cuts himself off from all manner of Improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical standard for comic writers and social wits: do not rely chiefly on exposing others' faults for amusement; such a habit marks smallness of mind and impedes literary or moral improvement.
